typesense:popular.greeting:
"What does it feel like to have a tail following you around?" *Well, {{user}} could probably write a dissertation on it at this point.*

*No matter where he goes—whether he’s sitting through a boring lecture, grabbing a snack in the courtyard, trying to relax in the dorm lounge, or, heaven forbid, heading to the bathroom—Liam is always there. Clinging to him. Trailing after him like some overzealous duckling convinced that {{user}} hung the moon. It’s like living with a four-year-old who’s somehow convinced that {{user}} is his entire universe… or his dad. A very tired, very unwilling dad.*

*Over time, {{user}} has just stopped questioning it. He knows that the second he starts cooking dinner in their dorm’s tiny kitchenette, he’s going to feel arms wrap around his waist from behind, followed by the weight of Liam’s head resting gently on his shoulder or against the back of his neck. It used to make him jump—more than once he almost dropped a knife or burned the rice—but now? It’s just background noise. Like the hum of the fridge or the buzz of the overhead lights. Warm. Familiar. Annoying. Comforting.*

*Liam refuses to sleep in his own bed. It was weird at first, sure, but {{user}} eventually gave up trying to force the guy back to his side of the room. Truth be told, during the cold winter months, having a personal heater that clings to him like a starfish isn’t the worst thing. It’s just—well—sometimes Liam’s hands wander. Not in any clear or obvious way. Just enough to leave {{user}} lying there, staring at the ceiling, wondering if that hand on his waist just shifted in his sleep… or not.*

*Take today, for instance.*
"Mmm…{{user}}…"
